articles.title: New Starbucks Drive-Through Opens on Whitworth Road
articles.excerpt: A new Starbucks drive-through on Whitworth Road in Rochdale will open to the public on Friday, 7 August, following a soft launch attended by local dignitaries.
articles.content_html:
A new Starbucks on Whitworth Road in Rochdale will open its doors to the public on Friday, 7 August. The coffee shop is located near the Dunelm store and features both indoor seating and a drive-through service.

On Thursday, 6 August, the Mayor and Mayoress of Rochdale, along with representatives from Springhill Hospice, attended a soft launch for the new store. Guests were invited to visit the branch ahead of its official opening.

The new Starbucks is positioned close to Rochdale Infirmary and other businesses along Whitworth Road. Its location, combined with the option for customers to sit inside or use the drive-through, is expected to provide an additional venue for those visiting or waiting for the hospital.

The official opening is set for tomorrow, and the new branch aims to serve both local residents and visitors to the area.

articles.title: Lord-Lieutenant's visit, a surprise inspection passed and a packed cafe: quite a week for Whitworth's Stronger Together
articles.excerpt: The Whitworth carers' group welcomed the King's representative in Lancashire, retained its 5-star hygiene rating in a surprise inspection, and saw its Community Cafe overflow into the main hall — all in one week.
articles.content_html:
A remarkable week for Whitworth carers' group Stronger Together began with a royal representative at the door and ended with a cafe so busy it spilled into the main hall.

On Monday the group welcomed the Lord-Lieutenant of Lancashire, Amanda Parker, and her husband Robert. Mrs Parker is His Majesty The King's personal representative in Lancashire and the first woman to hold the role in the county in almost five hundred years, and her visit is a mark of how far the volunteer-run group has come.

The same day brought a test of a different kind: an unannounced visit from environmental health officers just before lunch service. The inspectors found everything in order and the group retained its food hygiene rating of 5, the top score, which it has held since Rossendale Borough Council first awarded it in December 2024.

By Tuesday the group's Community Cafe was packed, with every table full and half of the main hall pressed into service to seat everyone.

Stronger Together was founded in 2023 by Angela Forster and Kathleen Proctor, both unpaid carers themselves, after they found there was nowhere locally for carers to turn for support. What began as a weekly coffee morning has grown into something much bigger, now based at The Ashcroft on Market Street, where volunteers serve more than 70 fresh, home-cooked meals every week alongside cakes and unlimited drinks, all free of charge with donation pots for those who wish to give.

The group describes itself as a warm, safe space offering advice and emotional and practical support, with activities including prize bingo, crafts and quizzes, and it runs entirely on fundraising, raffles, donations and grants. A crowdfunded project launched last year added gentle exercise sessions with a qualified trainer, healthy eating advice and a singing group open to all ages and abilities.

Recognition has followed. The founders received a Mayor's Special Award at the Whitworth Business and Community Awards in 2023, with the then Mayor of Whitworth describing the pair as truly inspirational to the community. The group went on to win the Not-for-Profit category at the Rossendale Business Awards, and this summer it was shortlisted for Community Group of the Year at the Pride of Rossendale Awards.

Reflecting on the week, the founders thanked the group's volunteers and supporters, saying the group is truly blessed in the people around it.

Anyone who would like to support Stronger Together, volunteer or find out about its sessions can contact the group through its Facebook page.

articles.title: STYFC Reserves Lose 4-2 to Peterlee Town at Whitworth Academy
articles.excerpt: STYFC Reserves faced a disappointing defeat against Peterlee Town, ending the match 4-2 at Whitworth Academy, despite some positive moments in their performance.
articles.content_html:
A football match at Whitworth Academy saw STYFC Reserves lose 4-2 to Peterlee Town. The match, played under the lights, was marked by a slow start for the home team, which allowed Peterlee to take an early lead.

STYFC Reserves fell two goals behind before managing to respond with some positive play. Despite the disappointing result, the team noted that there were aspects of their performance that could be built upon in future matches.

The defeat leaves STYFC Reserves looking to regroup and improve as they prepare for their next fixture. The team will be keen to learn from this experience and work on their game ahead of upcoming challenges.

Fans and supporters will be hoping for a turnaround in form as the season progresses, with the next match providing an opportunity to bounce back.

articles.title: Peaceful Pool sessions return to Whitworth Leisure & Wellbeing Centre for SEND families
articles.excerpt: Whitworth Leisure & Wellbeing Centre is once again offering its popular Peaceful Pool sessions throughout the summer holidays, creating a calm, welcoming and sensory-friendly swimming environment for children and adults with SEND and their families.
articles.content_html:
Families across the Rossendale Valley and Rochdale borough are being invited to enjoy a quieter, more inclusive swimming experience this summer as Whitworth Leisure & Wellbeing Centre continues its popular Peaceful Pool sessions.

Designed specifically for children and adults with Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), along with their families, the sessions provide a calm, judgement-free environment where everyone can relax, connect and enjoy time together at their own pace.

The initiative recognises that many families can find busy public swimming sessions overwhelming due to noise, bright lighting and sensory stimulation. Peaceful Pool aims to remove those barriers by creating an environment where participants feel comfortable, supported and included.

Sessions will take place every Thursday from 11:30am until 1:00pm throughout the six-week summer holidays.

To create a more accessible experience, the pool environment will feature reduced lighting to provide a calmer atmosphere, while sensory toys and floating aids will be available for swimmers to enjoy. Families are encouraged to use the facilities in whatever way feels right for them, whether that means swimming, playing in the water, paddling at the poolside or simply becoming familiar with the environment.

Organisers say the sessions are all about allowing people to be themselves without fear of judgement.

The promotional campaign explains that many families of children with SEND can often feel judged or cautious about how their child's behaviour may be perceived in public spaces. Peaceful Pool has therefore been designed to offer a welcoming environment where everyone can feel safe, respected and accepted.

The centre's message is simple: 'Everyone is welcome here just as you are.' That philosophy reflects a growing recognition across the leisure sector of the importance of making public facilities more inclusive and accessible for people with additional needs.

Swimming is widely recognised for its physical and mental wellbeing benefits, helping to improve confidence, mobility, coordination and overall fitness while providing an enjoyable activity for the whole family. Creating opportunities for families to access those benefits in a supportive environment can make a significant difference for many people who may otherwise struggle to attend mainstream sessions.

The Peaceful Pool sessions are available at the standard swim admission price, ensuring families can take part without paying a premium for accessible provision.

Whitworth Leisure & Wellbeing Centre continues to expand its programme of community-focused activities, with Peaceful Pool forming part of its wider commitment to ensuring local leisure facilities are welcoming and inclusive for residents of all ages and abilities.

Peaceful Pool takes place every Thursday between 11:30am and 1:00pm throughout the six-week summer holidays at Whitworth Leisure & Wellbeing Centre.

articles.title: Whitworth pub praised for exceptional Sunday roast
articles.excerpt: A pub on Whitworth Road has been praised for its Sunday roast, with one customer declaring it the best they have ever had while dining out.
articles.content_html:
A pub on Whitworth Road has received praise for its Sunday roast. A customer shared their experience on social media, stating it was the best beef roast they had ever enjoyed while dining out.

The post included a message of appreciation to a friend, highlighting the quality of the meal and the overall dining experience at the establishment.

The Albion pub has become a popular choice for locals seeking a hearty Sunday meal, contributing to the community's dining options.

As more patrons share their positive experiences, the pub is likely to see an increase in visitors looking to enjoy a similar meal.
